selection, review uses your default category. `--items <comma-separated-ids>`
selects particular entries; `--json` returns machine-readable results. The command
prints the Cockpit link for continuing the conversation and reviewing proposals.
Use `sk intake default --category research` to change your personal default,
`sk intake move --item <id> --category research` to organize an entry, and
`sk intake discard --item <id>` or `sk intake restore --item <id>` to change its
review state. These actions preserve the original clip and never admit knowledge.

The proposal shows its sources, exact text and knowledge destination. An existing
destination keeps its topic assignment. For a new destination, include the topic
category or `domain:<slug>` tag in the reviewed proposal so the resulting knowledge
can appear in the intended repository briefing. Changing that assignment requires
reviewing the changed proposal. After confirmation, run `sk agent briefing --json`
to check `knowledge_sources`, then search for the accepted material. The original
clip remains linked. A new session loads the updated briefing.

### Verify an installed intake API

During intake development, `bun run verify:intake` runs the focused type,
domain, HTTP, briefing, MCP, and CLI checks, including a real local
PostgreSQL/API smoke flow. It avoids the repository-wide test suite. Use browser-use
with Codex or Claude Code for browser journeys; visual acceptance is performed manually.

`bun run verify:intake-live` checks a selected server through its public API.
Set `SK_ENGINE_URL` and `SK_INTAKE_TEST_KEY` outside the repository. The default
run is read-only and reports compatibility, readiness and the delivered archive.
It is separate from the local `bun run verify` gate.

For a synthetic write check, use a dedicated test tenant and its user key:
add `--allow-writes --test-tenant-id <uuid> --run-id <unique-run-name>
--json <report-path>`. The tenant must match the authenticated identity. The
check collects in its own category, tests exclusion before confirmation and the
exact proposal, and verifies that the API key cannot confirm it. The report's
`handoff.review_url` opens the proposal in the Cockpit, where a person of that
tenant confirms it. Then run the same command with `--after-confirm --proposal-id <id>`
to check the single admission, provenance, search and the domain briefing.
It reports timings and retained resource IDs. Intake has no deletion API, so
test records remain for inspection. This API check does not measure model
judgment or replace a real browser/chat verification. It never deploys code.

## License

MIT

## Build asset verification

Engine builds fetch the embedding model from the immutable revision in
`vendor/embedding-assets.json`. Every model and ONNX runtime asset must match its
recorded byte length and SHA-256 checksum, including files already cached locally.
Downloads replace an existing file only after verification; unexpected runtime
package contents fail the build. Valid cached assets do not require a network fetch.

Embedding inputs are limited to 8,192 characters before tokenization so large
API catalogs cannot monopolize the engine's event loop. Full documents remain
stored and available to text search; this limit applies only to vector generation.
Background embedding processes one text at a time and yields between texts so
HTTP requests can run during a backfill.

When intentionally updating the model or runtime dependency, verify the upstream
revision, license and asset provenance before updating this manifest. Do not accept
a newly downloaded checksum merely to clear a failed build. Asset-manifest changes
also invalidate the local demo build receipt.

## Sandbox data tools

JavaScript workflow transforms can use bounded, synchronous `sk` helpers. They
perform no network, filesystem or credential access. Namespaces are immutable.
Promises and unseeded randomness are unsupported; use the execution clock and
`sk.uuid()` for repeatable values.

| Task | Helpers | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Decimal amounts | `sk.money.add/sub/mul/div/round/compare` | Decimal strings; `div` and `round` require scale and `down`, `halfUp`, `halfEven` or `up`. No currency conversion. |
| CSV | `sk.csv.parse/stringify` | Explicit delimiter/header options; export escapes spreadsheet formulas by default. Up to 10,000 rows. |
| Dates | `sk.date.parse/format/add/startOf/convertZone` | Date-only values stay dates. Local datetimes require an IANA zone; ambiguous or missing DST times require explicit `earlier`/`later`. |
| Validation | `sk.schema.validate/assert`, `sk.assert` | Local schema references only; no remote resolution or asynchronous validators. |
| URLs | `sk.url.parse/build/query/encode/decode` | WHATWG parsing, repeated query entries, UTF-8 percent encoding. No requests. |
| XML | `sk.xml.parse/build` | Ordered `{name, attributes, children}` trees retain mixed text; no DTD or custom entities. |
| Text and records | `sk.template.render`, `sk.diff.records` | Escaped HTML by default, explicit text mode; bounded list sections. Record diff requires a unique key. |

```javascript
return {
  total: sk.money.add("19.90", "4.95"),
  csv: sk.csv.stringify([{ name: "Ada", amount: "24.85" }]),
  tomorrow: sk.date.add("2024-02-28", 1, "days"),
  greeting: sk.template.render("Hello {{name}}", { name: "Ada" })
};
```

Text inputs and outputs are limited to 1 MiB, structures to 100,000 nodes and
64 levels. Existing sandbox memory, execution and output budgets still apply.
Each helper is embedded and loaded on first access in each sandbox;
regenerate it with `bun run gen:sandbox-tools` and check it with
`bun run check:sandbox-tools-drift`. Package versions and timezone data are pinned
in the lockfile. These tools do not add document rendering, OCR or a browser.
JavaScript transforms, JSONata and binary parsing use bounded worker processes.
The default lane can run two workers in parallel; hooks have a separate lane.
Per-engine-process global and per-tenant queue limits apply across default and
hook workers.
The RSS watchdog is available on Linux; it is a polling limit rather than a
kernel-enforced memory ceiling.

## Runtime measurements

`bun run benchmark:runtime:smoke` records local correctness, latency, throughput,
fault recovery and sampled process-family memory. Use
`bun scripts/runtime-benchmark.ts compare --baseline <baseline.json> --candidate <candidate.json> --output <directory>`
to produce JSON, HTML and SVG evidence. Retain the original source, lockfile and
runtime with each baseline; do not compare measurements from different machines.

`bun run benchmark:runtime:full` uses five repetitions, a 60-second warmup and
180-second measurement windows at concurrency 1, 4, 16 and 64. Reference performance
acceptance requires Linux x64, four CPUs and at least 8 GiB RAM. Local smoke
results do not establish that acceptance. Tail percentiles require adequate
samples; errors and timeouts remain in the report. Read each report's coverage
and environment limitations before interpreting a pass.

`bun run benchmark:runtime:release` captures a candidate only; it does not issue a
release verdict. It focuses on the eight release-gated JavaScript
and JSONata measurements, with five repeats, a two-second warmup and a 30-second
measurement window per run. Run paired baseline and candidate captures with
`bun scripts/runtime-benchmark.ts paired --profile release --baseline-source <baseline-checkout> --candidate-source <candidate-checkout> --output <directory>`
on the same reference machine. Capacity acceptance requires p95 no higher than
100 ms at concurrency one and four, at least 100 successful operations per second
at concurrency four, no errors, timeouts or rejections, 10,000 sampled successful observations and five paired repetitions for each
gated measurement, on both baseline and candidate. This is an explicit fixed
capacity budget, not a measurement of production load. The report separately
preserves the historical relative latency and throughput comparison:
per-call process isolation has an unavoidable transport cost, so that comparison
remains evidence of a tradeoff rather than the release-capacity decision. The
reference-machine requirement and every correctness check still apply. Latency
samples use a bounded deterministic reservoir; event counts and throughput use
all observations. A paired or compare command exits unsuccessfully on failed or
inconclusive acceptance; the short smoke in `bun run verify` checks correctness
and transport recovery but does not establish release capacity.
Before `bun run release:tag`, set `SUBKIT_RUNTIME_BASELINE_MANIFEST` and
`SUBKIT_RUNTIME_CANDIDATE_MANIFEST` to the retained paired reference manifests.
The tag command requires a passing capacity comparison and verifies that the
candidate runtime-source subset and lockfile hashes match the checkout being released.

# sk CLI reference

Every `sk` command and argument — and the surface authoring runs through:
creating or changing a workflow, connector, knowledge source or skill is a
definition edit, and definition edits belong here, where the change is a
file you can read and a command you can re-run.

Running bare `sk` opens the interactive REPL; every command below is
scriptable and prints to stdout. The declarative path — `create --file`,
`update --file`, `validate`, `preview` / `probe` — checks a definition
*before* it exists rather than after, so a mistake costs an error message
instead of a half-built connector someone has to clean up.

The `requires` column is the persona-aware *visibility* gate used for
`--help` filtering — the engine independently enforces permissions on
every API call.

| command | requires | description | subcommands |
| ------- | -------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| `sk agent` | `skill:read` | Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup | `briefing`, `capture`, `init` |

| `sk init` | — | Complete first-run engine bootstrap (consumes the token printed at engine boot) | — |
| `sk install` | `connector:write` | Guided setup for enterprise integrations | `github`, `google-workspace`, `hubspot`, `jira`, `salesforce`, `slack`, `teams` |
| `sk intake` | `intake:read` | List collected items and start a selected Chat review | `default`, `discard`, `list`, `move`, `restore`, `review` |
| `sk invites` | `identity:read` | Manage user-provisioning invites | `list`, `revoke` |
| `sk join` | — | Redeem an invite to provision your personal API key (no login required) | — |

| `sk logout` | — | Drop the active profile | — |
| `sk logs` | `audit:read` | Tail the engine's runtime log ring. --follow streams via SSE; --since accepts 5m / 2h / 1d / ISO-8601. | — |
| `sk ls` | — | List cached conversation sessions for the active profile | — |
| `sk mcp` | — | Run a stdio MCP server proxied to the engine | — |

## Commands and arguments

Every argument of every command. `<name>` is positional; `--name` is a flag.

### `sk agent`

Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup

#### `sk agent briefing`

Print or verify the domain-scoped session briefing for coding agents

- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .sk/agent.json of the repo; without hooks, else the known domains the repository name names)
- `--budget` (string) — Token budget for the briefing
- `--hook` (default: false) — Hook mode for Codex and Claude Code: inject a repository briefing and show a non-blocking status or warning
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk agent capture`

Send a session transcript to the engine to collect learnings for review

- `--transcript` (string) — Path to the transcript file (JSONL or text)
- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .sk/agent.json of the repo)
- `--agent` (string, default: claude-code) — Producing agent name
- `--session-id` (string) — Session id for evidence attribution
- `--hook` (default: false) — SessionEnd/Stop-hook mode: read hook JSON from stdin, never fail
- `--detach` (default: false) — Process the hook payload in a detached process
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk agent init`

Set up automatic SubKit briefings for this repository in Claude Code and Codex

- `--domains` (string, required) — Comma-separated domains for this repository (e.g. accounting, blog-de)
- `--budget` (string) — Optional token budget for each briefing
- `--skip-claude` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.claude/settings.json
- `--skip-codex` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.codex/hooks.json


### `sk apikeys`

Manage API keys

#### `sk apikeys create`

Issue a new API key (shown once)

- `--name` (string) — Friendly key name (label)
- `--expires` (string) — Expiry — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (e.g. "workflow:read,workflow:run"). Defaults to your own credential's scopes; ["*"] (full role-derived access, and read-and-execute over MCP) only when your credential has no scope limits. Add "mcp:authoring" for a key that may also author definitions over MCP (a coding agent); leave it off for a key going into a browser client.
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".

#### `sk apikeys list`

List API keys

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk apikeys revoke`

Revoke an API key

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id

#### `sk apikeys rotate`

Rotate an API key (new key shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id


### `sk apps`

The apps that sign their users in and call SubKit (products settings, sign-in providers, workflows, users, budget); erase-user removes one app user's SubKit data

#### `sk apps erase-user`

Erase an app user: removes SubKit's own data about that person for this app; the account at the sign-in provider stays. Irreversible

- `<app>` (positional, required) — App id (the product_id)
- `<user>` (positional, required) — User id (listed by sk apps show <app>)
- `--yes` (default: false) — Confirm the erasure without asking
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk apps list`

List the apps of this workspace with environment, users, budget today and readiness

- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk apps show`

Show one app: settings, sign-in, workflows, users, today's budget and readiness with the next action

- `<id>` (positional, required) — App id (the product_id)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `sk attach`

Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut)

- `<conversation-id>` (positional, required) — Conversation id (UUID)
- `<path>` (positional, required) — Path to file
- `--content-type` (string) — Override detected MIME type
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link
- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `sk audit`

Query the append-only audit log

#### `sk audit export`

Stream audit log as NDJSON to stdout or a file

- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--output` (string) — Output file path (default: stdout)

#### `sk audit query`

Filter the audit log

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp or relative (e.g. 10m, 1h, 7d)
- `--action` (string) — Action name filter
- `--actor` (string) — Actor id filter
- `--resource-id` (string) — Filter by resource id
- `--cursor` (string) — Continue after a previous page (its next_cursor)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk audit show`

Fetch one audit event by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Audit event id


### `sk auth`

Start a connector's browser sign-in and print the URL to open. Works for every connector that signs in with an account — a web service or an MCP server; the engine names the route.

- `--connector-id` (string, required) — Connector to reauthenticate
- `--json` — Emit the full response as JSON


### `sk branding`

Read, update, reset, or download tenant branding

#### `sk branding get`

Read tenant branding

- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`

#### `sk branding logo`

Download normalized branding logo PNG

- `<theme>` (positional, required) — light or dark
- `--output` (string) — Output file, defaults to stdout
- `--revision` (string)
- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`

#### `sk branding reset`

Reset branding at an expected revision

- `<revision>` (positional, required)
- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`

#### `sk branding update`

Replace branding from canonical JSON body (file or - for stdin)

- `<input>` (positional, required) — JSON file or -
- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`


### `sk categories`

Show and rename the catalog categories shared by every kind

#### `sk categories list`

List the catalog categories with how many workflows, connectors, knowledge sources, skills and files use each

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk categories rename`

Rename across all kinds with revision checks; preserve purpose ownership and merge into an existing target

- `<from>` (positional, required) — Current category
- `<to>` (positional, required) — New category
- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk chat`

Manage external chat spaces (Google Chat / Slack)

#### `sk chat install-space`

Register a chat space with the engine (Google Chat / Slack)

- `<platform>` (positional) — google_chat | slack
- `<workspace_id>` (positional) — Native space id, e.g. spaces/<id> (Slack: team id T…)
- `--bot-token` (string) — Slack bot token (xoxb-…) — required for slack
- `--default-channel` (string) — Optional default channel
- `--as` (string) — Installer platform user id (auto-filled from a pending space when omitted)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk chat remove-space`

Remove a chat-space install

- `<id>` (positional) — Chat workspace row id
- `--yes` — Skip confirmation
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk chat spaces`

List chat spaces installed in this tenant

- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk clipper`

Install the Chrome clipping extension

#### `sk clipper install`

Install the local Chrome clipping extension

- `--dir` (string) — Installation directory
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine address (default: active profile)
- `--open` (default: true) — Open Chrome extensions after installing


### `sk connector-templates`

Manage connector templates

#### `sk connector-templates create`

Create a connector template

- `--file` (string) — Path to a full template JSON file
- `--slug` (string) — Template slug (short-form convenience mode)
- `--name` (string) — Template name (short-form convenience mode)
- `--driver` (string) — Driver identifier (short-form convenience mode)

#### `sk connector-templates delete`

Delete a connector template

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Template id

#### `sk connector-templates list`

List connector templates

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connector-templates recipe`

Show one recipe by slug (template slug + recipe slug)

- `<slug>` (positional) — Template slug (e.g. stripe)
- `<recipe>` (positional) — Recipe slug (e.g. list-customers)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connector-templates recipe-pack`

Show the recipes in a vertical pack

- `<vertical>` (positional) — Vertical (revops | customer-success | finance | data | devops | security | marketing | hr | solutions)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connector-templates recipes`

List recipes shipped with a connector template

- `<slug>` (positional) — Template slug (e.g. stripe, github)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connector-templates search`

Fuzzy-search connector templates by name/alias/keyword

- `<query>` (positional, required) — Search text (e.g. 'hub')
- `--limit` (string, default: 10) — Max results
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connector-templates set-oauth`

Store tenant-scoped OAuth client credentials for a connector template

- `--slug` (string, required) — Template slug
- `--client-id` (string, required) — OAuth client id
- `--client-secret` (string, required) — OAuth client secret


### `sk connectors`

Manage connectors

#### `sk connectors create`

Create a connector from a template slug (--template) or a definition file (--file). --file runs validate and probe against the unsaved definition first, so a broken connector is never created; pass --skip-checks to bypass.

- `--template` (string) — Template slug
- `--file` (string) — Path to a connector definition JSON file
- `--credential` (string) — Path to a credential JSON file used to sign the pre-save probe. Never stored — attach the credential with `sk credentials set` after create.
- `--name` (string) — Override connector name (--template only)
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the checks (NOT recommended).
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk connectors delete`

Delete a connector

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id
- `--yes` — Skip confirmation

#### `sk connectors disable`

Disable a connector. It keeps its configuration and credentials and stops being offered for use.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors docs-delete`

Delete a connector doc

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `<doc-id>` (positional, required) — Doc id

#### `sk connectors docs-ingest`

Ingest docs from a URL into a connector

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--url` (string, required) — URL to ingest

#### `sk connectors docs-list`

List ingested docs for a connector

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connectors docs-search`

Ranked search over connector docs

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `<query>` (positional, required) — Search query
- `--limit` (string, default: 10) — Max results

#### `sk connectors enable`

Enable a connector (operator on switch)

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors get`

Get a connector by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors import`

Turn an API specification into a connector. Parses the spec, shows the draft it produced, then creates it after confirmation (--yes to skip). Nothing is saved until you agree.

- `--spec` (string, required) — Path to the specification file, or a URL / curl command (see --source)
- `--source` (string, required) — openapi | google_discovery | postman | har | graphql | graphql_introspection | curl
- `--name` (string) — Override the connector name
- `--environment` (string) — dev (default) or prod
- `--yes` — Create without asking (for non-interactive use)
- `--dry-run` — Print the draft and stop. Nothing is created.
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `sk connectors inspect`

Inspect a connector resource (alias of `get`).

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors list`

List connectors, grouped into catalog blocks

- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block
- `--driver` (string) — Only this driver: http, graphql, postgres, s3, mcp
- `--flat` — One flat table instead of grouped blocks
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connectors mcp-authorize`

mcp driver: begin the interactive OAuth 2.1 flow and print the URL to open in a browser.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors mcp-inspect`

mcp driver: force one handshake and list the tools, capabilities and instructions the remote actually serves.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id

#### `sk connectors patch`

Update a connector, from --file (a partial definition: only the fields it names change) or from --name, --description and --category. --file runs validate first.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--file` (string) — Path to a partial definition JSON file
- `--name` (string) — New name
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `sk categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--skip-checks` — Skip validation (NOT recommended).
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk connectors probe`

Probe a connector's upstream boundary. With an id, probes the saved connector (alias of `test`); with --file, probes an unsaved definition and saves nothing.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id
- `--file` (string) — Path to a connector definition JSON file — probes it without saving it
- `--credential` (string) — Path to a credential JSON file. Signs this probe only; never stored. Required when the definition's auth_type is not 'none'.
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `sk connectors promote`

Promote a connector and its credentials from DEV to PROD

- `<id>` (positional) — DEV connector id
- `--to` (string, default: prod) — Target environment (prod only)
- `--strategy` (string, default: copy) — Promotion strategy: copy or move
- `--idempotency-key` (string) — Stable retry key; generated when omitted
- `--yes` — Confirm a move without prompting
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk connectors test`

Test a connector connection (alias of `probe`). Exits non-zero when the probe fails.

- `<id>` (positional) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `sk connectors validate`

Check a connector definition file against its driver's config schema. Saves nothing, reaches no upstream.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to a definition JSON file
- `--json` — JSON-only output


### `sk credentials`

Manage connector credentials

#### `sk credentials delete`

Delete a credential

- `<credential-id>` (positional, required) — Credential id

#### `sk credentials list`

List credentials for a connector

- `<connector-id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk credentials rotate`

Rotate a credential

- `<credential-id>` (positional, required) — Credential id

#### `sk credentials set`

Attach a credential to a connector (scriptable; no conversation needed). Modes: bearer | header | query | basic | aws_sigv4 | signed_jwt | none.

- `<connector-id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--mode` (string, required) — bearer | header | query | basic | aws_sigv4 | signed_jwt | none
- `--private-key-file` (string) — signed_jwt: local PKCS#8 PEM file; contents are sent only to the credential endpoint
- `--token` (string) — Secret token (bearer mode)
- `--header` (string) — header mode: "Name=Value" (comma-separate multiple)
- `--query` (string) — query mode: "key=Value" (comma-separate multiple)
- `--username` (string) — basic mode username
- `--password` (string) — basic mode password
- `--access-key-id` (string) — aws_sigv4 access key id
- `--secret-access-key` (string) — aws_sigv4 secret access key
- `--session-token` (string) — aws_sigv4 optional STS session token
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the post-set connectivity probe
- `--json` — JSON-only output


### `sk diagnostics`

Engine diagnostics: errors, LLM status, setup validation

#### `sk diagnostics errors`

Show recent engine errors

- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--since` (string) — ISO timestamp lower bound
- `--trace-id` (string) — Filter by trace id
- `--tail` — Keep reading (not applicable — uses snapshot endpoint)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk diagnostics llm`

Show LLM diagnostics

_No arguments._

#### `sk diagnostics setup`

Validate engine setup

- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk discovery`

Manage discovery runs and artifacts

#### `sk discovery approve`

Approve a discovery artifact

- `<artifact-id>` (positional, required) — Artifact id

#### `sk discovery artifacts`

List artifacts for a discovery run

- `<run-id>` (positional, required) — Run id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk discovery create`

Start a discovery run from one or more files

- `--file` (string, required) — File path(s), comma-separated
- `--label` (string) — Optional label for the run

#### `sk discovery get`

Get a discovery run

- `<run-id>` (positional, required) — Run id

#### `sk discovery list`

List discovery runs

- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk discovery reject`

Reject a discovery artifact

- `<artifact-id>` (positional, required) — Artifact id
- `--reason` (string) — Rejection reason


### `sk doctor`

Diagnose engine connectivity, authentication, and setup. Exits 0 (ok or warn) or 2 (blocked).

- `--engine-url` (string) — Override the resolved engine URL
- `--api-key` (string) — Override the resolved API key
- `--profile` (string) — Use a named profile
- `--json` — Emit one JSON object instead of human output


### `sk events`

Query audit events

#### `sk events get`

Get an audit event by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Event id

#### `sk events list`

List audit events

- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--since` (string) — ISO timestamp lower bound
- `--action` (string) — Filter by action
- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk executions`

Manage workflow executions

#### `sk executions abort`

Abort a running execution

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id

#### `sk executions get`

Get an execution by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON-only (skip Output files line)

#### `sk executions list`

List executions

- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--status` (string) — Filter by status
- `--source` (string) — Filter by request source (e.g. scheduler, cli, api, mcp, chat)
- `--parent` (string) — Lineage filter: list the reruns spawned from this execution id
- `--from` (string) — Only runs that started at or after this instant (ISO-8601 or now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — Only runs that started before this instant (exclusive; default: open)
- `--cursor` (string) — Continue after a previous page (the next_cursor it printed)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk executions rerun`

Re-run a previous execution against the workflow + input it carried. Useful after diagnose/repair.

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id to rerun
- `--input` (string) — Override the original input (JSON string). Omit to reuse it verbatim.
- `--follow` — Queue the rerun and stream its progress live (step-by-step JSON lines).

#### `sk executions result`

Print the final output a workflow execution produced

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON-only output

#### `sk executions steps`

List steps for an execution

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk executions tail`

Stream live output from an execution

- `<id>` (positional) — Execution id


### `sk extract`

Extract structured data from a file (LLM for text, native parsers for binary)

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to sample file
- `--hint` (string) — Hint to the LLM extractor (text inputs only)


### `sk files`

Manage files (upload, download, link, …)

#### `sk files delete`

Soft-delete a file

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--force` (default: false) — Skip confirmation prompt

#### `sk files download`

Download a file by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--output` (string) — Output path (default: ./<filename>, '-' for stdout)
- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output

#### `sk files get`

Show file metadata

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk files link`

Attach a file to an owning resource (conversation, knowledge_source, …)

- `<fid>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--to` (string, required) — Owning resource as <resource_type>:<id>
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link

#### `sk files list`

List files

- `--status` (string) — Filter by status (pending|ready|failed|…)
- `--linked-to` (string) — Filter to files linked to <type>:<id> (e.g. conversation:abc-…)
- `--cursor` (string) — Pagination cursor
- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows (1-100)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk files patch`

Rename a file or change its description or category

- `<id>` (positional, required) — File id (fid_…)
- `--filename` (string) — New filename
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `sk categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `sk files stats`

Aggregate file counters for this tenant

- `--by` (string) — Group by: status|scanner_verdict (default: status)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk files upload`

Upload a file (inline ≤5 MB, authenticated streaming above)

- `<path>` (positional, required) — Path to file
- `--content-type` (string) — Override detected MIME type
- `--no-dedup` (default: false) — Skip the client-side sha256 dedup probe (forces an upload)
- `--link-to` (string) — After upload, link the file to <resource_type>:<id>
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link
- `--label` (string) — Reserved for future labels (no-op today)
- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output (also silences progress)


### `sk health`

Runtime posture: liveness, token budget, failing runs, risk signals, schema drift, and process runtime. Use `sk doctor` for connectivity/setup.

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--window-hours` (string) — Lookback window for failing runs (default 24)
- `--json` — JSON output (composite object)


### `sk hooks`

Manage inbound webhook bindings

#### `sk hooks create`

Create an inbound webhook binding. The signing secret is read from a file (or - for stdin), never from an argument.

- `--slug` (string, required) — Public path: POST /v1/hooks/<slug>
- `--workflow-id` (string, required) — Workflow id to bind
- `--verifier` (string, default: standard) — Signature scheme: standard | github | stripe | hmac
- `--secret-file` (string, required) — File holding the shared signing secret (- reads stdin)
- `--config-file` (string) — JSON file for native_verifier_config, e.g. {"hmac": {...}} for the hmac verifier

#### `sk hooks delete`

Delete an inbound webhook binding

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Hook id

#### `sk hooks get`

Get an inbound webhook binding

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Hook id

#### `sk hooks list`

List inbound webhook bindings

- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk init`

Complete first-run engine bootstrap (consumes the token printed at engine boot)

- `--token` (string) — One-time bootstrap token printed by the engine on first boot
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL (defaults to http://localhost:3000)
- `--profile` (string) — Profile to write the new admin key into (default: default)
- `--admin-email` (string) — Admin user email (skip prompt)
- `--tenant-name` (string) — Tenant display name (skip prompt)
- `--llm-provider` (string) — LLM provider: mock|anthropic|openai|gemini|azure|bedrock|vertex (skip prompt)
- `--llm-api-key` (string) — LLM API key (skip prompt)
- `--llm-model` (string) — Model id the key is checked with and saved as llm.model (Azure: deployment name; needed for azure and bedrock)
- `--defaults` — Never prompt: fill anything still missing with local defaults (mock LLM provider, tenant 'Local', admin email from git config)

### `sk knowledge-sources`

Manage knowledge sources

#### `sk knowledge-sources analyze`

Generate a description + tags for a knowledge source via the engine LLM

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id
- `--force` (default: false) — Overwrite an existing description

#### `sk knowledge-sources create`

Upload a file as a knowledge source

- `--file` (string, required) — Path to file
- `--name` (string) — Source name (defaults to the filename)
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `sk categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated tags. When set, they are authoritative (no AI auto-tagging). Omit --description and --category to let the engine describe the source.
- `--scope` (string) — Scope: global | workflow
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Workflow id (required when scope=workflow)
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk knowledge-sources delete`

Delete a knowledge source

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id

#### `sk knowledge-sources get`

Get a knowledge source by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id

#### `sk knowledge-sources history`

Show a knowledge source's content versions (newest first)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id
- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk knowledge-sources import`

Import a directory of markdown files as one knowledge source (upsert by slug; OKF-compatible frontmatter is read tolerantly)

- `<dir>` (positional, required) — Directory to import
- `--name` (string) — Source name (defaults to root index.md H1 or dirname)
- `--slug` (string) — Stable slug (defaults to slugified name)
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `sk categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated extra tags (frontmatter tags merge in)
- `--scope` (string) — Scope: global | workflow
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Workflow id (required when scope=workflow)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk knowledge-sources list`

List knowledge sources

- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk knowledge-sources patch`

Update a knowledge source

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id
- `--name` (string) — New name
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `sk categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated tags (replaces existing)
- `--status` (string) — Status: active | inactive

#### `sk knowledge-sources restore`

Restore an earlier content version; the result is a new version

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Knowledge source id
- `--to` (string, required) — Version number from `sk knowledge-sources history`
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `sk knowledge-sources search`

Semantic search across knowledge sources

- `<query>` (positional, required) — Search query
- `--tags` (string) — Comma-separated tags to narrow results
- `--limit` (string, default: 10) — Max results
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `sk login`

Authenticate against a subkit engine

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — Scripted API-key login (skips device flow)
- `--tenant` (string) — Active tenant id
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name (~/.sk/config.json)
- `--portal-token` (string) — Authenticate as a portal-token principal


### `sk logout`

Drop the active profile

- `--profile` (string) — Profile name to clear (default: active)


### `sk logs`

Tail the engine's runtime log ring. --follow streams via SSE; --since accepts 5m / 2h / 1d / ISO-8601.

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key (audit:read required)
- `--profile` (string) — Use a named profile
- `--follow` (alias -f) — Live SSE tail (Ctrl-C to stop)
- `--since` (string) — Start time — relative (5m, 2h, 1d), ISO-8601, or unix-ms
- `--limit` (string) — Max entries when not following (default 200)
- `--module` (string) — Filter by module name (e.g. migrate, scheduler)
- `--action` (string) — Filter by action (e.g. drift_detected)
- `--level` (string) — Minimum level (trace|debug|info|warn|error|fatal)
- `--json` — Emit raw NDJSON for piping to jq, instead of pretty-printing


### `sk ls`

- `--all` — Show every profile, not just the active one

### `sk settings`

List, read, write, or interactively configure engine settings (secrets always masked)

#### `sk settings configure`

Interactive Ink palette for inspecting settings (← / → cycles tabs, type to filter in Config, Enter to edit, Esc to exit). In non-TTY environments use --non-interactive to print the JSON contract instead.

- `--tab` (string) — Open directly on a tab: Status | Config | Usage | Skills | Knowledge
- `--non-interactive` — Skip the Ink renderer; print the GET /v1/settings response as JSON. Auto-detected when stdin is not a TTY.
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk settings get`

Read one leaf by dotted path

- `<path>` (positional, required) — Setting path (e.g. llm.api_key)
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk settings list`

List every leaf with its resolved value

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk settings set`

Write one leaf. <value> must be valid JSON ('"abc"', 42, true, null).

- `<path>` (positional, required) — Setting path
- `<value>` (positional, required) — Value as JSON
- `--force` — Bypass requiresRestart guard in production
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--tenant` (string) — Tenant id (writes a tenant overlay)
- `--json` — JSON output

### `sk stats`

Tenant-scoped runtime statistics (needs stats:read)

#### `sk stats chat`

Chat turns, modes, deduplication, and outcomes

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--traffic-class` (string) — organic|synthetic|internal (comma-separated; default organic)
- `--operation` (string) — Filter canonical operation(s)
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter outcome(s)
- `--request-source` (string) — Filter request source(s)
- `--platform` (string) — Filter platform(s)
- `--response-mode` (string) — json|sse|sync|async|none

#### `sk stats connectors`

Connector-call volume + latency + outcome. Example: sk stats connectors --bucket hour --from now-24h

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--connector-id` (string) — Filter by connector id
- `--connector-slug` (string) — Filter by connector slug
- `--driver` (string) — Filter by driver (comma-separated)
- `--method` (string) — Filter by method (comma-separated)
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter by outcome (success,denied,error)
- `--status-class` (string) — 2xx,3xx,4xx_other,4xx_auth,4xx_rate_limited,5xx,network_error,no_status
- `--include-endpoint` — Add normalized endpoint-path axis

#### `sk stats conversations`

Conversation calls, streams, disconnects, and outcomes

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--traffic-class` (string) — organic|synthetic|internal (comma-separated; default organic)
- `--operation` (string) — Filter canonical operation(s)
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter outcome(s)
- `--request-source` (string) — Filter request source(s)
- `--platform` (string) — Filter platform(s)
- `--response-mode` (string) — json|sse|sync|async|none

#### `sk stats events`

Audit-event volume by class (webhook_outbound, webhook_inbound, chat, notification, schedule, self_healing, discovery, execution_lifecycle, policy, external_write). Example: sk stats events --class self_healing --bucket day --from now-7d

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--class` (string, required) — One of: webhook_outbound, webhook_inbound, chat, notification, schedule, self_healing, discovery, execution_lifecycle, policy, external_write
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter by outcome (success,denied,error)

#### `sk stats executions`

Workflow run volume + duration distribution. Example: sk stats executions --bucket hour --from now-24h

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Filter by workflow id
- `--status` (string) — Filter by status (comma-separated: succeeded,failed,…)
- `--request-source` (string) — Filter by request source (open set, e.g. api,scheduler,wait_reaper)
- `--execution-mode` (string) — dev|prod

#### `sk stats http`

HTTP route volume, latency, bytes, and errors

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--traffic-class` (string) — organic|synthetic|internal (comma-separated; default organic)
- `--operation` (string) — Filter canonical operation(s)
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter outcome(s)
- `--request-source` (string) — Filter request source(s)
- `--platform` (string) — Filter platform(s)
- `--response-mode` (string) — json|sse|sync|async|none

#### `sk stats llm`

LLM token usage + cache-hit + latency. Example: sk stats llm --bucket day --from startOfMonth

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--model` (string) — Filter by model (comma-separated)
- `--flow` (string) — Filter by flow (comma-separated)
- `--user-id` (string) — Scope to one user (another user needs stats:read:all)
- `--mine` — Scope to your own usage (resolves your user id automatically)

#### `sk stats mcp`

MCP JSON-RPC, sessions, capacity, tasks, and SSE

- `--bucket` (string) — minute|hour|day|month|year
- `--from` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (now-24h, now-7d, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — ISO-8601 or relative (default: now)
- `--tz` (string) — IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--group-by` (string) — comma-separated group dimensions (≤2)
- `--json` (default: false) — raw JSON output
- `--traffic-class` (string) — organic|synthetic|internal (comma-separated; default organic)
- `--operation` (string) — Filter canonical operation(s)
- `--outcome` (string) — Filter outcome(s)
- `--request-source` (string) — Filter request source(s)
- `--platform` (string) — Filter platform(s)
- `--response-mode` (string) — json|sse|sync|async|none

#### `sk stats operations`

The Übersicht's operations figures: runs, success rate, healthy connectors (now), applied repairs. Example: sk stats operations --window 7d

- `--window` (string) — 24h (default), 7d or 30d
- `--from` (string) — Window start (ISO-8601 or now-24h, startOfMonth)
- `--to` (string) — Window end (default: now)
- `--json` — Emit the raw engine response


### `sk status`

Print the active profile + engine reachability

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key (Bearer)
- `--tenant` (string) — Active tenant id
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name (~/.sk/config.json)


### `sk subscriptions`

Manage event subscriptions

#### `sk subscriptions create`

Create a subscription

- `--event` (string, required) — Event type
- `--workflow-id` (string, required) — Workflow id

#### `sk subscriptions delete`

Delete a subscription

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id

#### `sk subscriptions deliveries`

Show deliveries for a subscription

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id

#### `sk subscriptions get`

Get a subscription

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id

#### `sk subscriptions list`

List subscriptions

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk subscriptions patch`

Update a subscription

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id
- `--active` (string, required) — Set active state (true|false)

#### `sk subscriptions replay`

Replay a subscription delivery

- `<sub-id>` (positional, required) — Subscription id
- `<delivery-id>` (positional, required) — Delivery id


### `sk system`

Engine process operations (restart)

#### `sk system restart`

Restart the engine so a saved restart-sensitive setting takes effect (needs a supervisor)

- `--wait` — Wait (up to 240 s) until the restarted engine runs the saved settings
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name
- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk system-accounts`

Manage system accounts

#### `sk system-accounts create`

Create a system account

- `--name` (string, required) — Account name

#### `sk system-accounts delete`

Delete a system account

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Account id

#### `sk system-accounts list`

List system accounts

- `--json` — JSON output


### `sk tenants`

List tenants you belong to or switch the active one

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key (Bearer)
- `--tenant` (string) — Active tenant id
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name (~/.sk/config.json)
- `<use>` (positional) — Tenant id to switch to


### `sk update`

Update sk CLI to the latest version

- `--force` (default: false) — Force re-download even if already up to date
- `--check` (default: false) — Check for updates without installing
- `--channel` (string, default: stable) — Release channel: stable | beta
- `--rollback` (default: false) — Restore the most recent retained sk binary
- `--to` (string) — With --rollback, the explicit version to restore (default: most recent retained)


### `sk users`

Manage identity users

#### `sk users create`

Create a user in the caller's tenant

- `--email` (string, required) — User email
- `--role` (string) — Role: admin|member|enduser (default member)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk users delete`

Delete a user

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id

#### `sk users get`

Fetch a user by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id

#### `sk users invite`

Issue a single-use provisioning invite for a user (token shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id to invite
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (default: your own credential's scopes; ["*"] only when your credential has no scope limits)
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs
- `--ttl` (string) — Invite lifetime in minutes
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk users list`

List identity users

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--app` (string) — Only users who signed in to this app (product_id, see sk apps list)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk users patch`

Update a user's role (admin only)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id
- `--role` (string, required) — New role: admin|member|enduser


### `sk workflows`

Manage workflows

#### `sk workflows create`

Create a workflow from a JSON file (--file) or a solution recipe (--from-recipe <slug>, see `sk connector-templates recipe-pack solutions`). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass.

- `--file` (string) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--from-recipe` (string) — Slug of a solution recipe; its connectors are bound to the ones you already have
- `--bind` (string) — With --from-recipe: bind connectors yourself, as <template or placeholder>=<connector id or slug>[,…]; needed for templates without a fixed address such as http
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run. With --from-recipe it defaults to the recipe's sample input.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk workflows delete`

Delete a workflow

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id

#### `sk workflows dry-run`

Preview a draft WorkflowDef by dry-running it via runExecution (source=draft). No persistence. Alias: dry-run.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string
- `--name` (string) — Optional label (goes to executions.source_ref)

#### `sk workflows get`

Get a workflow by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id

#### `sk workflows history`

List committed versions of a workflow

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk workflows invoke-snippet`

Emit a ready-to-paste, authenticated snippet to run a saved workflow from your own app or CI (curl/node/python).

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--lang` (string, default: curl) — Snippet language: curl (default), node, or python
- `--environment` (string, default: prod) — Where the call runs: prod (default) or dev. Printed as the x-subkit-environment header.
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk workflows list`

List workflows, grouped into catalog blocks

- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block
- `--connector` (string) — Only workflows using this connector (id or slug)
- `--flat` — One flat table instead of grouped blocks
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `sk workflows patch`

Change a workflow's name, description or category without saving a new version (the slug and its wf_<slug> tool stay as they are).

- `<workflow>` (positional, required) — Workflow id or slug
- `--name` (string) — New display name
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `sk categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk workflows preview`

Preview a draft WorkflowDef by dry-running it via runExecution (source=draft). No persistence. Alias: dry-run.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string
- `--name` (string) — Optional label (goes to executions.source_ref)

#### `sk workflows restore`

Restore a prior workflow version

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `<version>` (positional, required) — Version number

#### `sk workflows run`

Run a saved workflow, an inline draft definition, or a single step

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id or slug (omit when using --draft or --step)
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string. Prefix with `@` to read from a file (e.g. `--input @./payload.json`).
- `--input-file` (string) — Upload a file and substitute its ref into --input at key K. Format: K=<path>. Repeatable.
- `--draft` (string) — Path to a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (no commit)
- `--step` (string) — Path to a single StepDef JSON file (no workflow persistence)
- `--name` (string) — Optional label for --draft runs (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--slug` (string) — Optional workflow_slug for --step runs (cosmetic)
- `--follow` — Queue the run and stream its progress live (step-by-step JSON lines). Saved workflows only.
- `--idempotency-key` (string) — Make this trigger safe to repeat: a second run with the same key is not started, the first run's id comes back instead. Saved workflows only.

#### `sk workflows update`

Update a workflow from a JSON file (PUT the full definition). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass. An unchanged definition does not rotate a version.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--file` (string, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `sk workflows validate`

Validate a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (structural + step schema checks). No execution, no persistence.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON

<!-- Source: settings.md -->

# subkit runtime settings

Every value below lives in canonical runtime configuration and is editable via
the Cockpit, HTTP/MCP settings APIs, `sk settings configure`, or `sk settings set`. Per-tenant
overrides go into the file's `tenants` section and only honor leaves
tagged `scope=tenant`.

Path resolution: tenant overlay → global value → schema default. Environment
variables never set a runtime setting.

## log
Logging

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `log.format` | enum("dev" \| "pretty" \| "prod" \| "ndjson" \| "json") | `"ndjson"` | global | no | no | Log output format |
| `log.level` | enum("trace" \| "debug" \| "info" \| "warn" \| "error" \| "fatal") | `"info"` | global | no | no | Log verbosity |

## server
HTTP server

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.global_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling across hosted ingress per minute; zero denies hosted ingress |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.peer_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling per verified connection peer and minute; zero denies hosted ingress |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.principal_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling per authenticated principal and tenant per minute; zero denies hosted requests |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.tenant_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling per hosted tenant and minute; zero denies hosted requests |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.tenant_per_month` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request allowance per hosted tenant and UTC calendar month; zero denies hosted requests |
| `server.port` | number | `3000` | global | no | yes | HTTP port to bind (1..65535) |
| `server.public_base_url` | string | `""` | global | no | no | External-facing URL the engine resolves at. Used by /install, chat link replies, and OAuth2 redirect-URI synthesis. Required for any OAuth2 connector. |
| `server.restart_supervised` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no | A supervisor (systemd with Restart=on-failure, Docker with a restart policy) starts the engine again after it ends. Enables POST /v1/system/restart (exit code 75). |
| `server.root_redirect_to_cockpit` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no | Redirect GET / to /cockpit with a non-cacheable temporary redirect. Disabled by default to preserve the HTML and Markdown engine entry point. |
| `server.trusted_proxy_hops` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Trusted reverse-proxy hops counted from the right of X-Forwarded-For; zero ignores forwarding headers. |
| `server.trusted_proxy_ips` | array | `[]` | global | no | no | Exact trusted reverse-proxy socket peer IPs. Every configured forwarding hop must match; X-Real-IP is never trusted. |

## database
Database connection

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `database.connect_timeout_ms` | number | `10000` | global | no | yes | Deadline for acquiring or establishing a PostgreSQL connection. |
| `database.idle_timeout_ms` | number | `30000` | global | no | yes | Time before an unused pooled connection is closed. |
| `database.keepalive_delay_ms` | number | `10000` | global | no | yes | Initial TCP keepalive delay for PostgreSQL connections. |
| `database.pool_max` | number | `10` | global | no | yes | Maximum application connections per pool and replica. |
| `database.query_timeout_ms` | number | `150000` | global | no | yes | Client-side PostgreSQL query deadline in milliseconds. |
| `database.statement_timeout_ms` | number | `120000` | global | no | yes | Server-side PostgreSQL statement deadline, initialized on each session. |
| `database.url` | string | `—` | global | yes | yes | Bootstrap-only Postgres connection string. Rotate DATABASE_URL and restart replicas; runtime revisions cannot change this binding. |

## llm
LLM configuration

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `llm.api_key` | string | `""` | tenant | yes | no | Primary LLM API key |
| `llm.context_1m` | boolean | `false` | tenant | no | no | Enable 1M context window where supported |
| `llm.critic.enabled` | boolean | `false` | tenant | no | no | Run the second-stage LLM critic on workflow drafts after every static gate passes |
| `llm.critic.max_consecutive_rejections` | number | `3` | tenant | no | no | After this many consecutive critic_rejected results in a conversation, skip the critic to avoid an infinite re-author loop |
| `llm.critic.min_steps` | number | `3` | tenant | no | no | Minimum step count for the critic to run on a draft (drift in recent drafts also triggers a run) |
| `llm.fallback_model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Fallback model identifier |
| `llm.fallback_provider` | enum("mock" \| "anthropic" \| "openai" \| "gemini" \| "azure" \| "bedrock" \| "vertex" \| "ai_gateway") | `null` | tenant | no | no | Fallback provider on primary failure |
| `llm.hosted.enabled` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no | Hosted paid-model service mode; requires tenant context independently of signup policy. |
| `llm.hosted.global_monthly_microunits` | string | `"0"` | global | no | no | Operator-owned global monthly hosted budget in USD microunits; zero blocks paid calls. |
| `llm.hosted.models` | json | `[]` | global | no | no | Exact provider:model allowlist with verified provider-enforced context maxima, including extended context, and maximum USD rates for every context tier. No paid native tools or multimodal inputs. |
| `llm.hosted.tenant_monthly_microunits` | string | `"0"` | global | no | no | Operator-owned monthly hosted budget per tenant in USD microunits; zero blocks paid calls. |
| `llm.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Primary model identifier |
| `llm.output_guard` | enum("soft" \| "hard" \| "off") | `"soft"` | global | no | no | LLM output safety mode (soft: rewrite + log, hard: throw, off: bypass — never use in production) |
| `llm.provider` | enum("mock" \| "anthropic" \| "openai" \| "gemini" \| "azure" \| "bedrock" \| "vertex" \| "ai_gateway") | `"mock"` | tenant | no | no | Primary LLM provider |

## Authentication providers

`auth.providers` is one atomic, validated runtime setting available through Cockpit, HTTP, MCP, `sk settings`, and the canonical config file. Records use `protocol: api_key` or `oidc`; one API-key adapter and multiple named direct OIDC adapters may coexist. Provider ids must be unique, and every OIDC callback is `/v1/identity/login/callback` on `server.public_base_url`. A successful write is active for subsequent browser-login requests without an engine restart.

OIDC records are public clients using Authorization Code with PKCE. Runtime configuration intentionally has no `client_secret` field and rejects one if supplied; use an issuer that supports public clients with `token_endpoint_auth_method=none`. The environment is not an auth-provider source.

Configured labels are diagnostic metadata only. The common `mcp-auth` surface derives its two user actions from protocol and always presents `Continue with SSO` before `Continue with API key`. Discovery exposes the canonical labels `SSO` and `API key`; no provider-specific route or parallel configuration tree is accepted.

<!-- Source: connectors.md -->

# Connector & recipe catalog

What ships in the box: **61 connector templates** across **16 categories**, carrying **247 recipes** — pre-authored, runnable workflows you clone instead of starting from a blank page.

A **template** connects a system: base URL, auth flow, endpoint schema, and a vendor-basics Skill. A **recipe** is a complete workflow shipped on that template — say what you want in a conversation and sk clones the closest recipe as your starting draft.

| **HubSpot** | `hubspot` | http | bearer | HubSpot CRM API |

| **Supabase (GraphQL)** | `supabase-graphql` | graphql | header | Supabase GraphQL API (pg_graphql at /graphql/v1) — one roundtrip for nested reads instead of N+1 PostgREST calls. |

## Recipes

Grouped by template. **Trigger** is how the workflow starts: `request` (on demand — chat, CLI, MCP, REST), `schedule` (cron), or `webhook` (an external system calls in). **Also uses** lists connectors beyond the template's own.

<!-- Source: transactional-email.md -->

# Transactional email replies

A Gmail request step may use the explicit `transactional_delivery` profile to
reply to the address in an original signed request. This is reusable for access
requests, registrations and other requested replies. Event names and field paths
are configurable; no website, product or applicant is built into the engine.
Fixed-recipient `report_delivery` continues to use its existing rules.

### Author the workflow

Use sensitive execution privacy, a strict input schema with bounded lengths and
one plain-text Gmail send step. Keep sender, connection and template in the
reviewed workflow; visitor input selects only the reviewed original recipient.
The payload must include its UUID and event type inside the signed JSON body.
For example, an event body with `event`, `reference` and `contact.address` can use:

```json
{
  "kind": "gmail_transactional",
  "webhook_id": "<reviewed-binding-uuid>",
  "event_type": "registration.requested",
  "event_type_input": "body.event",
  "request_id_input": "body.reference",
  "recipient_input": "body.contact.address",
  "from": "sender@example.test",
  "content_type": "text/plain",
  "max_body_bytes": 8192
}
```

Place the profile on the Gmail request step beside `max_retries: 0`. Its request
body must contain only `raw`. No pagination, fan-out, generic boundary, simultaneous
fixed-recipient profile, response selection or filtering is supported. Input paths
start at `body`, traverse own object properties and reject prototype keys. Choose
a request-byte ceiling from the bounded template, rather than the largest allowed
value. The ceiling measures serialized UTF-8 Gmail JSON, including base64 overhead.

### Bind and review

1. Create an active Standard Webhooks binding for this workflow in the same tenant.
   Configure exactly the reviewed event type and a dedicated signing secret. Never
   use skipped verification, a public API key or browser credentials.
2. Persist the request UUID and original payload before handoff. Send the UUID in
   both the signed body and `webhook-id`. Sign `id.timestamp.rawBody` and send the
   matching timestamp, signature and event-type headers. The event type also has
   to match the reviewed field inside the signed body: the header alone is unsigned.
3. Prepare and validate the workflow normally. The operator reviews the exact
   version, sender, connection, signed source and field paths, byte ceiling and
   run/time limits. A signature authenticates ingress; it does not grant effects.
   Do not force a sensitive workflow through a missing preparation or approve a
   static report recipient while actually addressing somebody else.
4. Activate only after those checks and the normal human execution-authority
   review. Confirm behavior with a controlled recipient, then connect the public
   form and verify the same request twice produces one message.

Separately managed inbound bindings remain independent of the definition's
trigger. Request or schedule activation removes only reverse-bound webhook
triggers; webhook activation updates only its own reverse-bound binding. It
never rewrites or removes CRUD bindings, their signing secrets or event filters.
Archiving or deleting a workflow still removes all its inbound bindings. After
activation, verify that the reviewed signed source is still present before
enabling a public form. A removed source requires a new binding and a normally
reviewed workflow version referencing its actual ID; never reuse a stale ID or
weaken signature verification.

At dispatch the engine rechecks authority, source provenance, active binding,
original input identity, actual MIME recipient/sender/type and request size. A
payload field pretending to be provenance is ignored. On-demand calls, child
workflows and concrete one-off tool approvals cannot substitute for the signed
admission and reviewed recurring authority. CC/BCC and extra recipient headers
are rejected. The outgoing request cannot follow redirects or retry automatically.

SubKit's existing signer uses the stored secret string verbatim as a UTF-8 HMAC
key. Compute HMAC-SHA256 over `id.timestamp.rawBody`, Base64-encode the result and
send `webhook-signature: v1,<base64>`. There is no automatic `whsec_` prefix removal
or Base64 key decoding. Match those exact key bytes in an external adapter; a
library's protocol name alone does not guarantee interoperability.

### Inspect outcomes

`GET /v1/workflows/{id}/transactional-mail-receipts?limit=20&offset=0` requires
`workflow:read` for that workflow. It returns request/execution/step IDs, state and
timestamps, with no applicant address or MIME. The public OpenAPI contract includes
this read operation. Audit also records reservation and settlement.

A reservation is written atomically before network access. Its unique key is the
tenant, workflow and original request UUID, across workflow versions and execution
IDs. It survives execution cleanup; workflow or tenant deletion removes it.
`sent` requires a successful Gmail response with a message ID and confirms API
acceptance, not inbox delivery. `attempted` and `delivery_unknown` require operator
inspection. A crash, timeout or ambiguous response never authorizes automatic
resend. This endpoint has no retry or reset operation. Producer handoff retries
keep exactly the same payload and ID, renewing only timestamp/signature; changed
content under a previously admitted signed ID is refused.

### Model and authoring behavior

The shipped workflow-authoring skill and webhook knowledge explain this profile,
its limits and refusal remedies. The generated agent documentation and OpenAPI
schemas describe the same contract. Confirmation of tenant knowledge remains a
human review step; source changes do not silently approve tenant material.
Tool palettes, including MCP workflow aliases, validate object schemas before invoking a provider. Incompatible
root combinators/references are omitted without weakening workflow validation;
use the generic workflow operation. Residual schema errors are classified as
schema incompatibility, not network/provider unavailability.

### Verification and release status

Source implementation is separate from release and deployment. Required checks
include unit schema/MIME contracts, real PostgreSQL signed-ingress and concurrent
reservation cases, tenant/permission receipt reads, existing fixed-recipient and
execution-authority regressions, AI contract checks and the repository quality
gate. Test-only transport replacements never constitute a real Gmail delivery.
A production claim additionally needs the released engine, migrated receipt table,
signed binding, reviewed active workflow, server secret provisioning and an actual
controlled end-to-end delivery. Website publication is a separate final step.

The existing Lovable website was published after controlled live acceptance on
2026-10-20. Contact and beta-request forms delivered both the operator notification
and localized acknowledgement through the reviewed Gmail workflow in preview and
on the public host. An identical repeated request created no additional execution.
[Website tasks](https://github.com/MikeBild/subkit/wiki/website-todo) and [Lovable setup](https://github.com/MikeBild/subkit/wiki/docs-lovable-setup) distinguish
this verified integration from remaining product, legal and distribution work;
operational evidence stays in the private handoff.
